items.title: Tracking down cellular gene functions with AI and microscopy
items.excerpt: LMU researchers (Cell) pair AI image analysis of ~70 million microscopy-imaged cells with CRISPR edits to spot visual changes caused by individual genes, then isolate those cells intact for protein-level study.

items.title: Largest 2D map of the universe helps scientists discover new gravitational lenses
items.excerpt: A residual neural network trained to spot subtle image patterns searched DESI Legacy Imaging Survey data for lens candidates; VLT/MUSE spectroscopy confirmed 70 new gravitational lenses for dark-matter and cosmology studies.

items.title: AI chatbots endorse existing climate-related policies twice as often as new proposals
items.excerpt: A University of Waterloo study (Environmental Research Communications) ran ~55,000 prompts through 11 LLMs and found they endorse current policies ~70% of the time vs ~34% for new proposals, a status-quo bias that could slow climate action.

items.title: Simple math formula predicts when AI chatbots will go rogue
items.excerpt: GWU physicists Neil Johnson and Frank Huo (Patterns) derive a formula from a single attention unit that predicts when a chatbot tips from acceptable to harmful output, matching 18 of 19 tipping cases across seven open models.

items.title: 'Make this face look gay': AI models alter faces to give people stereotypical 'gay,' 'straight' or 'criminal' features
items.excerpt: RIT researchers (EMNLP 2026) show GPT Image 1 Mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image refuse to judge a face's orientation but readily edit photos to look 'gay', 'straight' or 'criminal' using stereotyped features.

items.title: Spiking neural network learns to predict what will happen, when, and how likely it is
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo WPI-IRCN team (Communications Biology) builds a 1,000-neuron recurrent spiking network that learns with local rules which event to expect, when, and how likely, adapting as probabilities shift - a brain-inspired model of prediction.

history_match.title: Toward physical AI: When the hardware becomes the neural network

items.title: Introducing AlphaProof Nexus: An AI tool for formal mathematical proof discovery
items.excerpt: A Science paper reports AlphaProof Nexus, an LLM-based framework that autonomously seeks formally verified proofs and solved dozens of previously open problems across several fields; a Perspective by Avigad and Ballard notes even failed AI attempts aided human progress.

items.title: AI finds different recipes for carbon nanotube forests with matching structures
items.excerpt: A National Science Review study shows AI can identify several distinct growth recipes that reach the same carbon-nanotube array height, density and alignment, untangling interdependent process conditions for materials synthesis.

items.title: Using machine learning and computation to unveil mechanisms for CO2-to-fuel conversion
items.excerpt: Indian Institute of Science researchers (Nature Communications) built a machine-learning-driven framework that maps nearly 10,000 surface reactions in CO2 hydrogenation to methanol on copper, instead of hand-picking a few likely steps.

items.title: Mathematicians marvel, and grumble, at OpenAI's trove of new results
items.excerpt: Mathematicians' response to OpenAI's 'slop drop' of hundreds of results: several groundbreaking proofs, but how they were generated remains unclear. (Follow-up to the OpenAI math release - peer reaction angle.)

history_match.title: AI Has Solved One of Math's $1 Million Millennium Prize Problems

items.title: How AI helped bring an ancient tomb dating to before the Roman Empire back to life
items.excerpt: Researchers paired artificial intelligence with acoustic technology to reconstruct the Etruscan Tomb of the Blue Demons, recreating how the pre-Roman burial chamber looked and sounded.

items.title: Scientists are decoding elephant rumble calls, including 'greetings' and 'coos'
items.excerpt: A team used machine learning on hundreds of rumble recordings from Amboseli elephants to interpret whole choruses, linking low-frequency calls to behavioural contexts such as greetings.

items.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
items.excerpt: Mathematicians are facing AI's sudden advance with grief, anger and a search for fresh ideas: 'If we don't adapt, there's just no more math in 50 years.'

items.title: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability
items.excerpt: DOE announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects, its national AI-for-science program to accelerate discovery across the national labs.

items.title: Hybrid Digital Twins Developed for Future Autonomous Labs
items.excerpt: A hybrid digital twin that combines mechanistic modeling with artificial intelligence could enable autonomous, self-driving biomanufacturing labs.

history_match.title: Tumor digital twins: from months to minutes with AI

items.title: Now in Nature: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
items.excerpt: The technique behind Bolmo, Ai2's fully open byte-level language models, is now published in Nature, with new checkpoints showing the approach generalizes beyond Olmo to other model families.

items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for protecting wildlife, from drone surveys to automated species detection.
